results.title: AWS Lambda Pricing
results.content:
Lambda Event Functions are priced based on the number of requests served and the duration your code runs, measured in GB-seconds. You choose the memory allocated to your function and get proportional CPU and resources. The free tier includes one million requests and 400,000 GB-seconds per month.

...

You can allocate any amount of memory to your function between 128 MB and 10,240 MB, in 1 MB increments.

results.title: AWS Lambda: pricing, memory and how to cut the bill
results.content:
### Requests and duration in Paris

Duration tiers apply "to aggregate monthly duration of your functions running on the same architecture (x86 or Arm, respectively), in the same region, within the account", so a large account pays less per GB-second as its month grows:

Lambda Event Functions in Paris (eu-west-3): requests and duration

| Item | List price | Unit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Requests | | |
| Requests, x86 | $ 0.20 | /M req per million requests |
| Requests, Arm | $ 0.20 | /M req per million requests |
| Duration, x86 | | |
| First 6 billion GB-seconds a month | $ 0.0000166667 | /GB-s per GB-second |
| Next 9 billion GB-seconds | $ 0.000015 | /GB-s per GB-second |
| Over 15 billion GB-seconds | $ 0.0000133334 | /GB-s per GB-second |
| Duration, Arm | | |
| First 7.5 billion GB-seconds a month | $ 0.0000133334 | /GB-s per GB-second |
| Next 11.25 billion GB-seconds | $ 0.0000120001 | /GB-s per GB-second |
| Over 18.75 billion GB-seconds | $ 0.0000106667 | /GB-s per GB-second |

USD, before tax. AWS Price List, eu-west-3, offer file published October 14, 2026, fetched October 15, 2026.
